newsitem.title: USA: Cool, dry weather seen for U.S. Midwest this week.
newsitem.headline: Cool, dry weather seen for U.S. Midwest this week.

text.p: U.S. meteorologists see cooler temperatures and clear skies for much of the U.S. Midwest in the next two days before a chance for scattered rains returns by the end of the week.
"We're seeing fair skies and temperatures warming in the western areas like Iowa and Nebraska," said Larry Mack, forecaster with Weather Services Corp. in Lexington, Mass.
High temperatures on Tuesday and Wednesday should be in the 80s degrees Fahrenheit in the western Corn Belt, while the eastern Corn Belt will see highs in the upper 70s, Mack said.

Forecasters see a limited chance for rain for much of the Midwest this weekend, but a cold front moving into the northern Plains and northern Midwest could bring scattered coverage of 30 to 40 percent on Saturday, forecasters said.
"I don't think it's going to be a big producer of rain," said Fred Gesser, meteorologist with Weather Express in Omaha, Neb.
The front is forecast to bring 0.25 to 1.5 inches of rain with 30 to 40 percent coverage favoring the Dakotas, the northern quarter of Iowa, and Wisconsin and Minnesota, Gesser said.
Central Illinois and Indiana, which are the areas considered most in need of rain, are unlikely to receive much precipitation until next week, forecasters said.
"Heat returns in the Missouri Valley portions of the Midwest and there is going to be a warm front coming north, but it will not influence Illinois," said Gesser with Weather Express.
He said that the next significant chance for rain for Illinois will not be until August 6 when a stronger cold front moves into the region.
